newsitem.title: USA: Georgia jobless rate rises to 4.7 pct for February.
newsitem.headline: Georgia jobless rate rises to 4.7 pct for February.

text.p: Georgia's unemployment rate rose to 4.7 percent in February after holding steady at 4.4 percent from November to January, state Labor Commmissioner David Poythress said.
That was up from 4.6 percent a year ago.
"The increase in the unemployment rate was expected," Poythress said. "The state's rate has risen from January to February for 19 of the past 20 years."
Poythress said the state's low unemployment rate and strong growth had encouraged more people to enter the job market in February.
"Over 20,000 more people found jobs during the month. But since it takes some people more than one month to find a job, 10,000 others were still looking for work," Poythress said.

After losing 80,000 seasonal jobs in January, the state gained back 16,000 in February, mostly in the service industries. The labor force rose by more than 30,000 over the month and 135,000 over the year to 3.81 million.
